newsitem.title: USA: Pontiac, Mich., forms commission on Silverdome.
newsitem.headline: Pontiac, Mich., forms commission on Silverdome.

text.p: The mayor of Pontiac, Mich. announced Thursday the formation of a commission to determine the best use for the Silverdome in light of the Detroit Lions football team's decision to seek a new stadium in Detroit.
"The Lions have indicated they will be exploring their options and we owe it to the citizens of Pontiac to do the same," said Mayor Walter Moore in a news release.

"We look forward to the Lions remaining in the Silverdome until their lease expires in 2004, but the commission will help us move forward and plan for what we think continues to be a bright future," he added.
The seven-member group appointed by Moore will spend the next year reviewing options for the Silverdome or its land, according to the release.

Last month, officials representing the Lions, Detroit and Wayne County announced they would build a $225 million domed stadium for the team as part of a downtown Detroit sports complex that would include a new ballpark for the Detroit Tigers baseball team.

Key to the plan would be the passage Nov 5 of a one percent lodging tax and two percent rental car tax in Wayne County. Revenues from the taxes would be used to back $80 million of county bonds for the project. The rest of the money would come from bond proceeds and other Detroit funds, contributions from the Lions and the local business community, and other sources.
The planned departure of the Lions from Pontiac has sparked several retaliatory proposals, including one that would require the team to repay a $13.9 million state subsidy.

The $50 million Silverdome was financed with proceeds from Pontiac stadium authority bonds and a 19-year state subsidy that totaled $13.9 million. About $23 million of Pontiac's bonds are outstanding, with $13.5 million maturing in 2004 and the remainder maturing in 2006.
